name: Acoustic mosquito sorter
subtitle: sound separates males for sterile-mosquito releases

effects.effect: a strong sound wave pushes steadily on objects

effect: a strong sound wave pushes steadily on objects
how: Releasing sterile male mosquitoes can crash the swarms that spread dengue and malaria, but every female must be removed first since females bite, and today's sieves and camera sorters are slow. Pupae float through a water channel crossed by standing ultrasound; the sound's steady push (acoustic radiation pressure) grows with size, so the bigger female pupae are steered to one outlet and the smaller males to another.
obstacle: Male and female pupae overlap in size, and even a few percent of females slipping through can spoil a release.
why: Faster sex-sorting is the bottleneck for sterile-mosquito programmes against dengue and malaria.
real: Mosquito pupa sex sorters use sieves, plates and machine vision (ORINNO, WOLBAKI, Science Robotics sorter); acoustic sorting found only for nematodes in microchannels.
